key_insight: Domain-specific biomedical transformer embeddings, especially BioBERT, improved detection of elevated dosing-error risk in clinical trial protocols.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help trial teams and regulators flag dosing issues earlier, supporting safer study design and oversight.
method: Encoded trial text with biomedical language models (ClinicalBERT, PubMedBERT, BioBERT, MedCPT).
Combined text embeddings with categorical metadata.
Compared classical ML and neural models using ROC-AUC for dosage-error prediction.
evidence_signal: BioBERT reached ROC-AUC 0.794 with logistic regression, and the best models achieved ROC-AUC 0.821 to 0.853 on the dosing-error task.
watch_item: Performance was measured on a predefined risk criterion, so real-world deployment would need external validation and careful threshold calibration.
paper_title: CaresAI at CT-DEB26: Detecting Dosing Errors In Clinical Trials Using Domain-Specific Transformer Embeddings and Classification Models
